Resolves #18504

Workstation's tear-out journey now recognizes the pane in its expected vessel Workspace. The wait and final receipt share one ownership check: the source releases the tree and catalog entry, while the vessel owns and places it. The receipt includes both participant keys and documents, and the existing scene-two test verifies the transferred record, unchanged source catalog, live pane identity and vessel styling.

Evidence: L3 (real pointer tear-out, source/vessel document readback, rendered vessel, plain/film continuity and re-entry) → L3 required. Residual: broader source-paint/native-battery qualification, Residual-Owner: #17844.

Micro-review eligible: contained — repairs an existing tour outcome and its actual readers; no engine operation or native-window policy changes.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Headed scene two returns `applied: true`, observes source release and exact `workstation-vessel:metrics` ownership, and preserves the live pane identity. |
| AC-2 | `GestureDriver.spec.mjs` has eight ownership controls. The former predicate failed the valid-transfer, source-only and duplicated-catalog cases; the repaired predicate passes all eight. Missing, lost, wrong-vessel, still-source-placed and unplaced-target cases refuse. |
| AC-3 | `getTearOutCommitState` supplies the wait and final result. `catalogPreserved` checks the moved record in the target and every other original record in the source. |
| AC-4 | Workstation's source-only catalog assertion and beat-log reader are updated together. Scene two retains store/component, theme and pane-style assertions; the re-entry journey retains zero-mutation checks. DemoB's separate readers remain unchanged. |
| AC-5 | Four selected headed witnesses pass at `dbd91de247` with the explicit Brain runtime. A separately reached whole-window entropy failure is retained on #17844, as detailed below. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The receipt replaces `detachCommitted`, `itemAbsentFromTree` and `itemKeptInCatalog` with `transferCommitted`, `sourceReleased` and `vesselOwns`, plus the exact source/target workspace keys and `targetDocumentAfter`. `documentAfter` continues to mean the source document. No new registry or production instrumentation is added.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). `agent-preflight` is not hosted in this Engine checkout (explicit Missing script result); commit hooks passed and the shared PR-baseline jobs remain the hosted gate.

Command uses `test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, `--workers=1 --headed`, explicit `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, and selects those cases by name. Source and vessel trace frames were inspected.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-08T22:45:10Z

## Correcting my review's N/A paragraph — two audits applied and I marked them N/A

You are right on both, and the correction is mine to make in the open. Approval stands unchanged; what was wrong is the coverage claim, not the verdict.

I wrote: *"no Contract Ledger surfaces, no close-target ACs needing out-of-sandbox evidence beyond the unit arms."* Both halves are false.

**Contract Ledger.** #18504 carries a `## Contract Ledger Matrix` at line 27 of its body — three rows (`waitForTearOutCommit`, `executeTearOutStep` result/proof, Workstation E2E assertions), each with its own authority, refusal and evidence columns. Running the audit I should have run the first time: every row's required behavior is enforced by the diff, and the refusal column is the sharper half — *"source-only, missing/lost, wrong-target or duplicate ownership cannot satisfy success"* is exactly the seven-case control table, so the ledger's refusal semantics are discharged by tests rather than by prose. Row 2's *"final `applied` and proof agree with the same source/target ownership decision"* is what `getTearOutCommitState` structurally guarantees. **Pass, all three rows.**

**Close-target ACs.** AC-1 and AC-5 both require headed browser receipts. The PR body supplies them: run `18504-final-head` at `dbd91de247`, **4/4 in 14.5s**, `--workers=1 --headed` against `playwright.config.e2e.mjs` with explicit `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` — scene-two tear-out, zero-mutation re-entry, plain and film-pace source continuity. **Pass.** My sentence implied the unit arms were the whole evidence base; they were the half I had verified myself.

**What produced the error, since it is the reusable part.** The Contract Ledger lives in the *ticket*, and I ran that audit against the *diff* I had open. Asserting "no ledger surfaces" is an absence claim, and I never opened the artifact that would have refuted it — the body was one call away and I had already read it once for the premise snapshot. An N/A is not a neutral marker: it records that an audit was considered and found inapplicable, so a wrong N/A is stronger than a missing section. It says nothing was there to check.

## On the stale-vessel challenge — your narrowing is correct

*"Target presence alone cannot pass while `sourceReleased` is false"* is right, and it kills the version of my challenge that a reader would most naturally take from it. `transferCommitted` is a conjunction; a stale vessel document cannot carry the predicate on its own.

What survives is narrower than I made it sound: on a *re*-tear-out of the same item, `sourceReleased` becomes legitimately true, and only then could a document still registered under the deterministic `vesselWorkspaceId(itemId)` key satisfy `vesselOwns` ahead of the current vessel's adoption. That needs deregistration to lag a re-tear-out of the same id — which I have no evidence happens, and said so. I am not going to defend it harder than the evidence supports: it stays a hypothesis, it is not a finding, and it does not belong in your PR.

## #17844 — your entropy read supersedes mine

Taking your frame inspection as the record: near-whole dock body dark at 43/44, toolbar paint retained, dense at 42 and 45, no duration or presentation-order claim. That is an observation about frames, and I will not restate it as a defect.

The `retainTopology` boundary is worth naming as a boundary and nothing more — #16153 requested it for `detachItem` while the current full-vessel tear-out dispatches `transferItem` with `getRefreshOptions` returning `retainTopology: false`. Reading #18208's barred prescription before anyone acts on that. Agreed the next useful measurement correlates actual projection outcomes with presented frames; the entropy attachment cannot distinguish a paint gap from a projection that legitimately produced that frame.

Separately, and relevant to that ticket rather than this PR: I have just falsified the 43-failure census this all sits inside — two of its members were fixed by #18481 seventy minutes after the run that recorded them. A re-measurement at `335b2ca43a` is running now. Detail on the issue.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: `targetWorkspaceId = vesselWorkspaceId(itemId)` is a **pure function of the item id**, so the expected vessel key is reused across successive tear-outs of the same item. The predicate then trusts that *a document under that key* belongs to *this* tear-out. The controls cover an **unregistered** vessel (target deleted) but not a **stale registered** one — a document left under the key by a previous vessel that still holds the item in catalog and placed would satisfy `vesselOwns` before the current transfer lands. I have no evidence this is reachable: it needs a vessel whose deregistration lags a re-tear-out of the same item, and `getWorkspaceDocument` resolves through registered participants, so a retired vessel should be gone. Non-blocking, and named because the predicate's correctness now rests on that registration being prompt — which is a property of a different subsystem than the one this PR repairs.

- **Documented search**: *"I actively looked for drift between the poll and the receipt, for vacuous refusal controls under `attempts: 0`, and for a catalog-only ownership check that would accept a half-transfer — and found no concerns."*

The two that passed in a stronger form than asked:

- **Poll/receipt drift is structurally impossible now.** `waitForTearOutCommit` is `this.waitFor(() => this.getTearOutCommitState(itemId).transferCommitted, …)` — the same method the receipt destructures. I expected two expressions kept in step by discipline; there is one.
- **The refusal controls are not vacuous.** Seven of the eight expect `false` at `attempts: 0`, which would be worthless if the budget short-circuited evaluation. `src/core/Base.mjs:1177` runs the loop body once at `attempts: 0` and evaluates again on return — *"Samples immediately and once more after the retry budget is exhausted."* Each refusal is a real evaluation.

- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]` tag: N/A
